html:
The Hungarian Revolution of 1956 was a nationwide revolt against the communist government and Soviet control, which began with a student march in Budapest on 23 October 1956 and was crushed by Soviet troops in early November.

Crowds pulled down a giant statue of Stalin, and fighting broke out at the radio building. Imre Nagy, a reform communist, became prime minister, promised free elections and announced that Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact. On 4 November Soviet tanks entered Budapest. About 2,500 Hungarians died, and some 200,000 fled abroad. Nagy was executed in 1958. The West did not intervene, a lesson for the Cold War. His reburial in June 1989 helped end communism in Hungary.
sum: The Hungarian Revolution of 1956 was a nationwide revolt against the communist government and Soviet control, which began with a student march in Budapest on 23 October 1956 and was crushed by Soviet troops in early November.
